summary: StratusPay persistent inflight-queue ACK-debt after multi-region failover causing duplicate completions and urgent customer escalation
description: Issue summary: Following an automatic multi-region failover (us-east -> eu-west) triggered by a noisy-host eviction, StratusPay observed a sustained window of duplicate completions and a spike in customer-facing 5xxs and streaming disconnects. Impact: Multiple customer flows returned duplicate responses and increased token billing; customer opened an urgent escalation requesting immediate mitigation and crediting guidance. Scope: ~3% of StratusPay production requests during the incident window (2026-03-12 02:13–02:42 UTC) experienced duplicate completions; incident affected two model families served from dedicated pools.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate region-level failover by cordoning primary GPU pool in us-east
2) Replay ~1k concurrent streaming requests with session affinity and prefix caching enabled
3) Observe inflight-queue growth in session-coordinator metrics and missed ACK deadlines
4) Note duplicate completions emitted when the backlog drains with stale cursor offsets
logs: 2026-03-12T02:15:11Z session-coordinator WARN: cursor_drift detected for session s_89f4, last_ack=2026-03-12T02:12:58Z
2026-03-12T02:17:33Z broker INFO: retransmit_count=4 for shard sh-3, ack-debt=512
Customer log excerpt provided: customer-request-id=sp-98123 duplicated response ids: [c91, c92]
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: broker ack-debt + session-coordinator cursor drift after failover amplified by continuous-batching causing replays
Evidence: metrics show sustained inflight_queue_size increase in session-coordinator and per-shard ack_deadline_missed spikes coincident with the failover event window
Tracer sample: request path shows service A re-enqueue -> service B deliver -> no ACK observed -> replay on reconnect
Reproduced in staging by artificially delaying ACKs from broker; duplicate completions correlate with stale prefix offsets in KV cache

Root cause: on failover we observed a race where in-flight stream leases were released but cursor offsets were not advanced in the session-coordinator; the broker retransmit logic then re-delivered completions without de-duplication checks
mitigations_applied: Hotfix deployed to session-coordinator to add transient lease marker and prevent immediate re-enqueue of recently-released cursors (rollback-safe) - deployed 2026-03-12T03:04Z
Emergency broker configuration change: reduce aggressive retransmit window from 2s -> 500ms to limit amplification - applied 2026-03-12T02:58Z
Customer-facing workaround: Support performed a targeted queue drain for StratusPay tenant and requested clients to replay only idempotent flows; credits offered for affected period

resolution_summary: Hotfix to session-coordinator plus broker retransmit tuning resolved the immediate duplication and streaming disconnects for StratusPay. Targeted tenant queue drain removed residual ack-debt. Customer was credited for impacted token billing and scheduled a postmortem call. A permanent de-duplication token and improved lease semantics are planned as next steps.
